entities.summary: Armenian studies or Armenology is a field of humanities covering Armenian history, language and culture. The emergence of modern Armenian studies is associated with the foundation of the Catholic Mechitarist order in the early 18th century. Until the early 20th century, Armenian studies were largely conducted by individual scholars in the Armenian communities of the Russian Empire, Europe, Constantinople and Vagharshapat in Armenia. After the establishment of Soviet rule, Armenian studies, and sciences in general, were institutionalized in Armenia and put under direct control of the Academy of Sciences. Armenian studies is a academic major.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Armenian studies played a significant role in preserving and promoting Armenian language and culture, particularly during the Soviet era when it was institutionalized in Armenia. This led to the development of modern Armenian literature and education.
